title: How do you justify it’s ok to use ai?
author: TechyCanadian
selftext:
Hi there,

I told my friends I wanted to use AI to make some games because it looks like a lot of fun. I started making something but when I shared this news, they were all shocked and highly pushed against me using ai for anything. 

In my mind I feel it’s ok, because lots of people will use it regardless to create what they imagine. They kept saying it’s stealing and there’s no skill, which I can understand the no skill aspect because it’s vibing basically. For me I just wanted to create what I imagined and of course I don’t take credit for the work because it was ai. What are your thoughts? Have you had people fight against you for using it?

comments.author: Double_Suggestion385
comments.body: Who cares, you can't control what idiots think.

comments.author: bettertagsweretaken
comments.body: Just create what you want to create. You don't have to share this with your current friends, or, you can use this as a gateway to find new friends who are more receptive to AI creations.

comments.author: Alternative_Sink9000
comments.body:
simply move along. You don't have to justify it, and you don't have to convince anyone. By the end of the day, whatever reasoning and evidence you shows to them will be forgotten by them anyway, they have their mind set on certain perspective, and it's hard to change.

  
Once you start using AI to make some games, you will then realize it's not as simple just "hi make me XX games with features YY with ZZ art"; no, you need a whole set of skills to make it right, to make it look consistent, and to squash any problem along the way. But do your friend even care about this? obviously not.

  
They will only realize when they try it themself, because for all I know, their mind is already set on rumors and hearsays.

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body: Yeah that’s fair too right, like sure we have to know how to prompt. There is a level of skill involved because you need to understand certain principles to get the results you want

comments.author: silvercoated1
comments.body: You do whatever you want. They don’t live for you

comments.author: iFart_69
comments.body: Don't tell .soon with dlss5 many will not know the difference

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body: So do you think I should tell them if they hate ai so much maybe don’t play games anymore because it’s all ai generated basically at that point

replies.author: jackadgery85
replies.body: Dlss5 is not ai generated game or art. It is ai enhanced lighting and textures

replies.author: iFart_69
replies.body: Dlss5 is trained/learned from existing video games hence works similar to AI. DL stands for deep learning

comments.author: nasir41
comments.body:
AI is here to stay. Even if we choose not to use it, 80% of others probably will.

From a business perspective, if I can get the same result in a few hours at 10% of the cost, instead of waiting days or weeks, why wouldn’t I use it? It means shipping faster, reducing costs, and staying competitive.

I completely understand people who prefer doing everything themselves because they enjoy the craft. There’s nothing wrong with that. But if you’re running a business, providing for your family, paying salaries, and competing in the market, results matter.

AI is a tool. The people who learn how to use it effectively will simply have an advantage over those who don’t.

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body: Completely agree.. it’s not going anywhere and it’s a powerful tool. I definitely plan to keep using it, thanks

comments.author: ADingoStoleMyLSD
comments.body:
Just ignore them, if you want to make something you've wanted to make then do it, I've buid things for myself to use to make my life better. 

Most the people who complain about AI killing creativity are wrong, these hings are supposed to take the tedious part out of creativity, so you can focus on the creative ideas. 

Build what you want and enjoy the thing you built, fuck other people's opinions.

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body: I agree and I tried to explain it’s similar to a good 3d printer vs a bad one.. I just wanted someplace I can create easily. My old printer kept having issues and breaking down so I couldn’t focus on what I love which is printing objects. My new printer allowed me to just build without all the troubleshooting

comments.author: CapitalDiligent1676
comments.body: Go for it! Designing a game is a creative endeavor. However, for the sake of transparency, I would point out that the graphic assets or programming were created using AI—after all, that’s standard practice even when using open-source graphic kits made by humans.

comments.author: thedev13
comments.body: Friends who push you down? Those ain't no friends.

comments.author: geldonyetich
comments.body:
I find it’s easier just to accept that, no matter what I do, I won’t be able to please everyone.

Some people will hate the tools you use, whether it’s AI or Unity.

Some people will hate the kind of game you want to make, even if it’s a well established niche.

Some people will find the art style appalling, even if it’s critically acclaimed.

Some people will hate you because you remind them of something they hate, and will hold onto that like it’s the only thing that matters to them.

But good news, none of that matters, because it was never your job to please everyone.

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body: Such a great perspective. We cannot please everyone. That’s very true, it’s not my job! Thank you.

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body:
China doesnt recognize copyright law the same as the western world. So china's AI is ok in that respect. Stole off the west? Oh well. Do something about it 🤣.

My point being, who cares? They just soubd like they're on the band wagon. AI isnt going anywherr

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: Artists repaint and sell famous works pixel for pixel even that is called imitation, not stealing. If AI art is stealing then AI code is stealing too and whenever you ask a question you're stealing from Encyclopedia Britannica etc. Just absurd.

comments.author: Constant_Physics8504
comments.body: Similar to how you justify not using it

comments.author: je386
comments.body: Don't justify. Just don't tell everybody that it's AI

comments.author: jackadgery85
comments.body:
Make a game to completion (including polish and marketing, then bug fixing once live), and then come back and say it's easy.

It's easy to tell a tool in plain english to make a dog fart when i press spacebar, or to make some 3d models. What isn't easy, and why every cunt isn't just doing this and getting rich, is creating fun game mechanics, interesting level design, and engaging stories, then marrying them all together in a way that ends up being fun and cohesive, **and then** understanding the human emotion behind the why in your polish and iterating, and being able to push through the very unfun last 20%, **and then** marketing your game, **and then** sifting through the feedback and decoding which pieces of feedback are genuinely things you should work on, and which are just noise because players are not designers.

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body: Fair points it’s about how they combine all together and the creativity in making good game dynamics. Well said 👍

comments.author: CourseSpare7641
comments.body:
When I see posts like this, I have to wonder how much life experience your friends have.  
  
Without giving too much away, in my career I've worked closely with the production teams in various industries.  
AI is integrated at virtually every point of the production chain across creative industries. Most managers mandate its use.    
  
Many creative companies now will not hire someone who is AI illiterate. 

Frankly OP, you would only be hurting your future career opportunities by being completely anti-ai. Look at it as a tool. It would not be helpful to act like its evil and unusable. Explore, build some experience, learn new skills. Don't burry your head in the sand.

replies.author: TechyCanadian
replies.body:
Thanks. Hard to say about their life experience, if I could comment I would say they are more closed off. 

Great perspective too and I agree that we should be comfortable with ai and using it.
